title: The 76 Refrigerators Zhang Ruimin Would Not Sell
conflicts: The 76 figure is identical in every account, but all trace back to Zhang or Haier; no 1985 contemporary report was found and the Irish Times (2019) calls it legend, so the story attributes the scene to Zhang's 2016 interview and says so. Who smashed the units differs: Zhang (2016) says each named worker smashed his own and he swung first; TIME (2014) says workers were handed hammers and Zhang smashed one; Irish Times says he smashed some and workers finished; Knowledge at Wharton (2001) says he smashed all 76 himself. The story gives Zhang's version and names the Wharton and TIME versions. Trigger: one customer's return (TIME, Gale) versus complaint letters (Haier timeline); both mentioned. 'Two years' wages' is quoted as Zhang's claim only.
notes: Company named 'Qingdao General Refrigerator Factory (later Haier)' as in the Wharton and Gale sources. Funding 'public' kept: the factory was owned by the city of Qingdao. Quote stance complicates (shame that leads to sin versus shame that is honour, beside the named notes and weeping workers).
